review_scope: Reviewed all 8 sparse contact-sheet pages covering 180 frames sampled every 45 seconds and all 33 dense contact-sheet pages sampled every 10 seconds. This remains a still-frame visual screening, not continuous audiovisual verification.

observations.description: Mikey and a woman are both visible at the desk from the start, with a persistent cutout image of another woman at upper left and a private-chat panel at right.
A vertical clip of a young man holding a phone appears at the opening and again from about 02:50 to 04:40, distinct from the two people at the desk.
The phone panel scrolls through a long private conversation with alternating green/grey bubbles, images, stickers, voice-message controls, and dates/times.
A green information-card/form graphic and adjacent screenshots are shown inside the conversation sequence; exact text is too small for reliable reading in the contact sheet.
The chat includes image thumbnails, a map/location screenshot, profile images, and short video previews, all apparently used to explain the case chronology.

The right panel changes from chat screenshots to a vertical video of a young man seated with a phone; ten-second frames and burned-in subtitles persist from about 83:50 to 102:50. This establishes a distinct third-party media segment, not whether its audio was audible to the stream.
The display returns to private chats with message bubbles and a visible 00:32 voice-message control while Mikey and the woman continue on set.
Near the end, another person or the seated woman stands/moves through the right side of the studio frame; the fixed sparse view does not establish whether speaking roles changed.

dense_review_windows.reason: Extended multi-person commentary over scrolling private chats, images, stickers, voice messages, and location/profile material; sender order and speaker mapping require denser review.
Inserted vertical video of a different man with subtitles; verify clip boundaries, whether its audio is played, and how Mikey and the woman frame or respond to it.
Return to private chat with voice-message material and multiple on-set people; verify exact speaker turns, playback, and case outcome claims.

attribution_limits: Mikey and a woman are simultaneously visible, so audio diarization must be mapped to the pictured speakers before assigning claims.
The persistent upper-left female cutout appears to be a graphic, not proof that the pictured person is present or speaking.
The young man in the embedded vertical video is a separate source/person; his subtitled statements must not be attributed to Mikey or the woman at the desk.
Private-chat text and voice messages belong to several parties; sender-side, playback, quoting, and commentary boundaries require continuous audiovisual checking.
Sparse frames do not establish consent, refusal, or behavioral outcomes even when surrounding conversation may discuss them.
privacy_or_third_party_risks: Private messages include avatars, text, timestamps, stickers, media, and possible voice recordings from third parties.
A third-party young man's face and speech appear in the embedded video sequence.
Map/location and profile-related screenshots may expose identifying or location information.
The persistent female cutout and other image thumbnails are third-party likenesses whose reuse rights and context are not established.

dense_observations.description: Mikey and a woman remain visible together in the studio through most of the review. A separate young man appears in embedded vertical media at the opening and again around 02:50-04:40; the upper-left woman remains a static cutout graphic.

From roughly 11:20 onward the right panel advances through alternating green and grey messages, stickers, photos, video previews, and voice or call-like entries. The side changes are visible, but they do not identify the people or prove who authored quoted material.

Around 52:00 a call-duration-like record appears inside the chat. It supports only that such a record is displayed; it does not establish who called, whether the call was played, or the substance of the call.

Around 68:50-74:50 the displayed evidence moves among media previews, a map/location-like screen, images, and short call-duration entries. These materials are third-party case evidence and may expose identity or location details.

A distinct young man occupies the embedded vertical video from about 83:50 to 102:50 and is shown holding a phone with burned-in subtitles. His visual presence is confirmed, but his audio, exact wording, and the hosts' agreement or criticism cannot be determined from still frames.
After the embedded video ends, the panel returns to chat and shows a 00:32 voice-message control among other private messages. The static control does not prove playback or speaker identity.

remaining_visual_limits: The dense review samples one still every 10 seconds; it is not continuous audiovisual verification and cannot map exact speaking turns between Mikey, the woman at the desk, and embedded sources.
The embedded young man's clip boundaries are visually narrowed, but whether its audio was played, paused, muted, quoted, endorsed, or criticized remains unresolved.
Small chat text, sender identities, message omissions, and playback-state changes between samples remain unreadable or unproven.
No consent, refusal, or behavioral outcome is visually established by the contact sheets alone.
